Rashi on Kiddushin 22a:11:1.hebrew: הוא ובניו עמו - על כרחיך בבני ישראלית, דאי בבני כנענית — ״האשה וילדיה״ כתיב (שמות כ״א:ד׳):
Rashi on Kiddushin 22a:11:1.english: He and his children with him - Perforce, [this refers] to the children of an Israelite woman; for if [it referred] to the children of a Canaanite woman, “The wife and her children [shall belong to her master]” is written (Exodus 21:4).

Rashi on Kiddushin 22a:12:1.english: That they are not fit to work and eat - For they are minors.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22a:13:1.hebrew: לאהדורי - לחזר על הפתחים, לפי שהיא בושה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 22a:13:1.english: To circulate - To go from door to door [begging], because she is embarrassed.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22a:1:1.english: Temutot - amortiysh in Old French (amortidish: dying [animals]).

Rashi on Kiddushin 22a:1:2.hebrew: וחשקת - בחשקו תלה הכתוב, ואפי' אינה נאה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 22a:1:2.english: “And you have a desire” - The verse made it dependent on his desire, even if she is not pretty:

Rashi on Kiddushin 22a:1:3.hebrew: ולא בה ובחברתה - שלא יקח שתים:
Rashi on Kiddushin 22a:1:3.english: But not her and her fellow - That he may not take two.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22a:2:1.hebrew: ליקוחין יש לך בה - קידושין תופסין, ואע"פ שהיתה עובדת כוכבים, שהרי אינה מתגיירת מדעתה:
Rashi on Kiddushin 22a:2:1.english: You have acquisitions [i.e., betrothal] with her - The betrothal takes effect, even though she was a gentile, since she does not convert of her own volition.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22a:2:2.hebrew: לך ולא לאחרים - שלא יקחנה לצורך אחרים, כגון אביו:
Rashi on Kiddushin 22a:2:2.english: To you, and not to others - That he may not take her for the needs of others, such as his father.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22a:2:3.english: That he not pressure her during the war - to have relations with her.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22a:3:1.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr> להאי ברייתא בספרי <abbr title="בפרשת">בפ'</abbr> ראה אנכי: "ואם אמר יאמר — עד שיאמר וישנה. אמר בתחילת שש ולא אמר בסוף שש — אינו נרצע, שנאמר: 'לא אצא חפשי' — עד שיאמר בשעת יציאה. אמר בסוף שש ולא אמר בתחילת שש — אינו נרצע, שנאמר: 'אם אמר יאמר העבד' — עד שיאמר כשהוא עבד". והכי פירושה: אמר ושנה שתי האמירות בתחילת שש ולא אמר בסוף שש — אינו נרצע, שנאמר: 'לא אצא' — משמע סמוך ליציאה. אמר שתי פעמים בסוף שש כו' — עד שיאמר כשהוא עבד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 22a:3:1.english: This is the version of this baraita in the Sifrei in Parashat Re'eh Anokhi: “’And if he shall say’ — until he says [it] and repeats [it]. If he said [it] at the beginning of six [years] and did not say [it] at the end of six [years], he is not pierced, as it is stated: ‘I will not go out free’ — until he says [it] at the time of leaving. If he said [it] at the end of six [years] and did not say [it] at the beginning of six [years], he is not pierced, as it is stated: ‘If the slave shall say’ — until he says [it] while he is [still] a slave.” And this is its interpretation: If he said and repeated the two statements at the beginning of six [years] and did not say [anything] at the end of six [years], he is not pierced, as it is stated: ‘I will not go out,’ which implies close to leaving. If he said [it] twice at the end of six [years], etc. — until he says [it] while he is [still] a slave.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22a:5:1.hebrew: ה"ג: אמר מר, אמר בתחילת שש כו', מאי איריא מלא אצא חפשי? תיפוק ליה דבעינן כו'! ותו: אמר בסוף ולא אמר בתחילת שש אינו נרצע, שנא' העבד — אטו סוף שש לאו עבד הוא? - והכי פירושה: אמר בתחילת שש כו' — קס"ד תחילת שש ממש. תיפוק ליה דבעינן אהבתי את אשתי ואת בני, ועדיין בתחילת שש אין לו אשה ובנים, שלא מסרו לו עדיין שפחה כנענית:
Rashi on Kiddushin 22a:5:1.english: This is the correct version: The Master said: “If he said at the beginning of six, etc., why specifically from ‘I will not go out free’? Let him derive it from [the fact] that we require, etc. And furthermore: If he said at the end and did not say at the beginning of six, he is not pierced, as it is stated: ‘The slave’ — is that to say he is not a slave at the end of six?” - And this is its explanation: “If he said at the beginning of six, etc.” — [the Gemara] assumed [this means] the literal beginning of the six [years]. [The Gemara asks:] Let him derive [that he cannot be pierced] from [the fact] that we require: “I love my wife and my children,” and at the beginning of the six [years], he does not yet have a wife and children, for they have not yet given him a Canaanite maidservant.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22a:6:1.hebrew: אטו סוף שש לאו עבד הוא - יום אחרון נקרא סוף שש, וכל היום הוא עבד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 22a:6:1.english: Is that to say [that at] the end of six [years] he is not a slave? - The last day is called "the end of six," and throughout the day he is a slave.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22a:6:2.hebrew: ה"ג אמר רבא בתחילת פרוטה אחרונה בסוף פרוטה אחרונה - ול"ג לא קשיא, ול"ג כאן. והכי פירושו: כל תחילת שש דקתני — כשמגיע להתחיל לסוף פרוטה אחרונה לפי חשבון גרעונה, שעדיין עליו שוה פרוטה, דהוי דמי עבד; וכל סוף שש (פרוטה אחרונה) — מאחר שהתחיל בה נקרא סוף, דלאו עבד הוא, דאין עליו שוה פרוטה. וה"ק: אמר בתחילת שש — קודם פרוטה אחרונה, דכבר יש לו אשה ובנים — ולא בסוף שש — לאחר שהתחיל פרוטה אחרונה — אינו נרצע, ואפי' אמר ושנה, דכתיב לא אצא חפשי, סמוך ליציאה, וכל זמן שיש עליו פרוטה שלימה לאו סמוך ליציאה הוא. אי אמר ושנה בסוף פרוטה אחרונה ולא אמר בתחילת פרוטה אחרונה — אינו נרצע, שנאמר אם יאמר העבד, עד שיאמר כשהוא עבד. ובלשון אחרת גירסא זו בפי כל, ואיני יכול להעמידה, שהרבה תשובות בה. וזה הלשון: אמר יאמר — עד שיאמר וישנה; העבד — עד שיאמר כשהוא עבד; אמר בתחילת שש ולא אמר בסוף שש — אינו נרצע, שנאמר אם אמר יאמר; אמר בסוף שש ולא אמר בתחילת שש — אינו נרצע, שנאמר לא אצא חפשי. והכי פירושו: אמר בתחילת שש פעם אחת ולא חזר ואמר בסוף שש — אינו נרצע, דבעינן אמר יאמר, שתי אמירות; אמר בסוף שש ולא אמר בתחילת שש — אינו נרצע, שנאמר לא אצא חפשי, וזה כבר יצא. השתא קשיא לי טובא: הא נמי תיפוק לי מאמר יאמר, דהא לא אמר ושנה! ואם באת לפרש אמר בסוף שש שתי פעמים — א"כ לא דמיא לרישא, דאי אומר בתחילת שש שתי פעמים מנא ליה דאינו נרצע? ועוד, מה לי דשבקיה לדרשה קמייתא דדריש העבד עד שיאמר כשהוא עבד, ונקיט ליה קרא אחרינא מלא אצא, והרי כבר יצא תיפוק ליה מהעבד:
Rashi on Kiddushin 22a:6:2.english: This is the correct reading: Rava said: At the beginning of the last peruta; at the end of the last peruta - And we do not read "There is no difficulty," and we do not read "Here." And this is its explanation: Whenever "the beginning of six" is taught, [it means] when he reaches the start of the final peruta according to the calculation of its reduction [in redemption value], for worth a peruta is still [incumbent] upon him, which constitutes the value of a slave; and whenever "the end of six" [is taught] (the last peruta), once he has begun it, it is called "the end," for he is no longer a slave, since worth a peruta is no longer [incumbent] upon him. And this is what it means: [If] he stated [this] at the beginning of six — before the last peruta, when he already has a wife and children — and not at the end of six — after he began the last peruta — he is not pierced, and even if he stated [it] and repeated [it]; for it is written: "I will not go free" (Exodus 21:5), [meaning] close to his departure, and as long as a full peruta is [incumbent] upon him, it is not [considered] close to departure. If he stated [it] and repeated [it] at the end of the last peruta, and did not state [it] at the beginning of the last peruta, he is not pierced, as it is stated: "If the slave shall say" (Exodus 21:5) — [meaning] only when he says [it] while he is [still] a slave. And in another phrasing, this version is in everyone's mouth, but I cannot sustain it, as there are many refutations against it. And this is its phrasing: "Saying, he shall say" [amar yomar] — until he says [it] and repeats [it]; "the slave" — until he says [it] while he is a slave; [if] he stated [it] at the beginning of six and did not state [it] at the end of six, he is not pierced, as it is stated: "If saying, he shall say"; [if] he stated [it] at the end of six and did not state [it] at the beginning of six, he is not pierced, as it is stated: "I will not go free." And this is its explanation [according to that version]: [If] he stated [it] at the beginning of six one time, and did not state [it] again at the end of six, he is not pierced, because we require "saying, he shall say" — two statements; [if] he stated [it] at the end of six and did not state [it] at the beginning of six, he is not pierced, as it is stated: "I will not go free," and this one has already gone free. Now, I have a major difficulty with this: This [case] too, let it be derived from "saying, he shall say," for behold, he did not say [it] and repeat [it]! And if you should come to explain that he stated [it] at the end of six two times — if so, it is not similar to the first clause; for if he says [it] at the beginning of six two times, from where does [the baraita] know that he is not pierced? And furthermore, why did it abandon the initial derivation, where it expounds "the slave" [to mean] until he says [it] while he is a slave, and took another verse, from "I will not go free"? Since he has already gone free, let it be derived from "the slave"!

Rashi on Kiddushin 22a:7:1.english: [If] he has a wife and children - [This refers to] a Canaanite maidservant who was given to him and bore him [children].

Rashi on Kiddushin 22a:8:1.english: Because he fares well - To exclude a sick person.

Rashi on Kiddushin 22a:8:2.english: Because he fares well - [This] excludes a sick person.

Tosafot on Kiddushin 22a:2:1.hebrew: ה"ג: שלא יקחנה לאביו ולא לבנו - ול"ג: "שתים, אחת לו ואחת לאביו, או אחת לו ואחת לבנו", דמאי איריא שתים? אפילו אחת לאביו נמי הוי איסור, דהא "לך" דרשינן:
Tosafot on Kiddushin 22a:2:1.english: This is the correct reading: "That he may not take her for his father or for his son" - And we do not read: "Two, one for him and one for his father, or one for him and one for his son." For why specifically two? Even [taking] one for his father is also forbidden, as we expound [the word] "to you" [to mean for yourself, and not for your father or your son].

Tosafot on Kiddushin 22a:2:2.hebrew: שלא ילחצנה במלחמה - פי' בקונטרס: לבוא עליה. משמע מתוך פירושו, דבמלחמה אסור לבוא עליה כל עיקר, ואפילו ביאה ראשונה אינו מותר עד לאחר כל המעשים. ותימה: א"כ, מאי קאמר "לא דברה תורה אלא כנגד יצר הרע"? כיון דבמלחמה אסור עד שיבא לביתו ולאחר כל המעשים, היאך נתפייס יצרו בכך? אכתי איכא יצר הרע במלחמה, ובביתו עד ירח ימים! ועוד קשה: אמאי קרי לה "בשר תמותות", כיון שנתגיירה? ועוד קשה מהא דאמר בפ' ב' דסנהדרין (דף כא.): תמר בת יפת תואר היתה, ולפיכך היתה מותרת לאמנון, כדכתיב: "דבר עלי אל המלך כי לא ימנעני ממך". ואם לא בא דוד על מעכה אם תמר עד לאחר כל המעשים, היאך היתה מותרת לאמנון? והרי אחותו מאביו היתה! שהרי אם תמר, לאחר כל המעשים, חשובה גיורת וליקוחין יש לו בה. דבשלמא אם נפרש דיפת תואר מותרת מיד — שפיר (דמי) מאי דקאמרה תמר: "כי לא ימנעני ממך", לפי שהיתה מותרת לו, דאיכא למימר שנתעברה אמה במלחמה, שעדיין היתה אמה עובדת כוכבים, וזו אינה חשובה כבתו של דוד, דאין בן הבא מן העובדת כוכבים קרוי בנך אלא בנה, דולד עובדת כוכבים כמותה; אבל לפירוש הקונטרס, שלא בא עליה עד לאחר כל המעשים, קשה כדפירשתי. ונראה לר"ת, דביאה ראשונה מותרת במלחמה, אבל ביאה שניה אסורה עד שתהא בביתו גיורת. [והא דקאמר "שלא ילחצנה" כו' — היינו להתחיל למנות ירח ימים, דאין יכול לדוחקה לעשות סדר הפרשה עד שתהיה בביתו]. ויש מיישבים פירוש הקונטרס, ולא קשה מידי מה שהקשה: "איך נתפייס יצרו", דאיכא למימר דבטל הימנו יצר הרע כיון שיש לו פת בסלו, שסופה להיות מותרת לו לאחר כל המעשים. ומה שהקשה: "אמאי קרי לה בשר תמותות כיון שנתגיירה", הא נמי לא קשה, דאיכא למימר לפי שמגיירה בע"כ ואינה גיורת גמורה, קרי לה "בשר תמותות". ומה שהקשה מתמר לא קשה, דאיכא למימר דתמר לא היתה בת דוד, אלא מקודם לכן היתה אמה מעוברת; והא דכתיב (שמואל ב י״ג:י״ח): "כן תלבשנה בנות המלך מעילים", לא משום שהיתה בתו, אלא לפי שגדלה בביתו של דוד עם בנות המלך. אך אין לתרץ שפיר לפירוש הקונטרס: מה חילוק בין ביאה ראשונה לשניה דמחלק גמרא לעיל? ומיהו אומר ר"י, דבירושלמי מצינו מחלוקת אמוראים בדבר זה; והכי איתא התם: רב אמר לא התיר אלא ביאה ראשונה, ואני אומר לא ביאה שניה ולא ראשונה הותרה אלא לאחר כל המעשים, כדכתיב: "ואחר כן תבא אליה ובעלתה":
Tosafot on Kiddushin 22a:2:2.english: "That he should not pressure her during the war" - Rashi explained: To engage in intercourse with her. It is implied from his explanation that during the war it is completely forbidden to engage in intercourse with her, and even the first act of intercourse is not permitted until after all the procedures [prescribed in Deuteronomy 21:12–13]. And this is astonishing: If so, why does [the Gemara earlier on 21b] say, "The Torah spoke only corresponding to the evil inclination"? Since during the war it is forbidden until he comes to his house and after all the procedures, how is his [evil] inclination appeased by that? There is still the evil inclination during the war, and in his house for a month of days! And furthermore, it is difficult: Why does [the Gemara] call her "meat of dying animals" [which is permitted only under duress as a concession], given that she has converted? And furthermore, it is difficult from that which [the Gemara] says in the second chapter of Sanhedrin (21a): Tamar was the daughter of a woman taken captive in war (yefat to'ar), and therefore she was permitted to Amnon, as it is written: "Speak now to the king, for he will not withhold me from you" (II Samuel 13:13). And if David did not engage in intercourse with Maacah, the mother of Tamar, until after all the procedures, how could she have been permitted to Amnon? Behold, she would have been his paternal sister! For the mother of Tamar, after all the procedures, is considered a convert, and he can form a valid marriage with her [so her offspring is legally his daughter]. For it is well if we explain that a yefat to'ar is permitted immediately [during the war]; then what Tamar said, "for he will not withhold me from you," is well understood as meaning that she was permitted to him, since one can say that her mother conceived her during the war, when her mother was still a gentile, and she [Tamar] was not considered David's daughter, as a child born of a gentile woman is not called your son/child, but her son/child, since the offspring of a gentile woman has her status. But according to the explanation of Rashi, that he did not engage in intercourse with her until after all the procedures, it is difficult as I explained. And it appears to Rabbeinu Tam that the first act of intercourse is permitted during the war, but a second act of intercourse is forbidden until she is in his house and a convert. [And that which it states: "that he should not pressure her, etc." — this means to begin counting the month of days, for he cannot press her to perform the sequence of the passage until she is in his house.] And some resolve the explanation of Rashi, and none of [the difficulties] that were raised are difficult at all: What was raised, "how is his [evil] inclination appeased?" — for one can say that the evil inclination ceases from him since he has "bread in his basket," for she will ultimately be permitted to him after all the procedures. And what was raised, "why does [the Gemara] call her 'meat of dying animals' given that she has converted?" — this too is not difficult, for one can say that because he converts her against her will and she is not a complete convert, [the Gemara] calls her "meat of dying animals." And what was raised from Tamar is not difficult, for one can say that Tamar was not the biological daughter of David, but rather her mother was pregnant from beforehand [from another man]; and that which is written (II Samuel 13:18): "For with such robes were the king’s virgin daughters appareled," was not because she was his daughter, but because she grew up in David's house with the king's daughters. However, one cannot well resolve according to the explanation of Rashi: What distinction is there between the first act of intercourse and the second, which the Gemara distinguishes above? Nevertheless, Ri says that in the Yerushalmi we find a dispute of Amoraim regarding this matter, and this is how it is stated there: Rav said: [The Torah] permitted only the first act of intercourse; and I say: Neither the second act of intercourse nor the first was permitted except after all the procedures, as it is written: "And afterward you may come to her and have relations with her" (Deuteronomy 21:13).
